$comment: CROSS-PLATFORM CONFORMANCE VECTORS for the thread-replies latest-N read model.
Contract: RFC 043 Appendix B §B.10 — getLatestNReplies / listenLatestNReplies.
Web and KMP run THIS SAME FILE (mobile syncs the bytes; a CI gate compares them
against the canonical copy on slock staging — NOT against a second hardcoded hash,
which would be a gate with the very blind spot it exists to catch).
FRAME SHAPE: each frame carries the AUTHORITATIVE replyCount from the server
(thread:updated spreads threadInfo). The model ADOPTS it and never derives it.
Deriving it (count + 1) double-counts once a reply has been EVICTED from the
N-window: a window-scoped identity check no longer sees the evicted reply, so a
replayed frame for it takes the 'new' branch. The window forgets; the server's
count cannot. Found by @Android-Developer-2 — see evicted_live_reply_replay_is_noop.
The invariants, and why each is silent when broken:
1. ORDER BY SEQ — a late frame carries an OLDER seq. A naive unshift promotes a
stale reply to 'newest' and the preview lies about what was said last.
2. DEDUPE BY IDENTITY against a FIXED seam — never by seq magnitude. A running
high-water mark discards a genuinely new reply that merely arrived out of
order (9 before 8), and it vanishes forever with no error.
3. NO-CHANGE => SAME REFERENCE — a value-only check passes an implementation that
rebuilds an equal object every frame, which then re-renders the whole timeline.

cases.name: late_frame_does_not_lead_the_window
cases.why: A frame older than the whole window must not enter it, let alone lead it.

cases.name: out_of_order_convergence
cases.why: THE permutation property. Any arrival order of the same frames must converge to the same window. This is the vector that caught the running-watermark bug.

cases.name: out_of_order_convergence_control_in_order
cases.why: Control for the above: the in-order permutation must produce an identical window.

cases.name: reconnect_replay_is_a_no_op
cases.why: On reconnect the server replays history. Without the seam these duplicate into the window and inflate replyCount.

cases.name: replay_then_genuinely_new_reply_still_lands
cases.why: The seam must not block real new replies that follow a replay.

cases.name: duplicate_message_id_dropped_even_with_higher_seq
cases.why: Identity dedupe, not seq dedupe: a re-delivered message must not appear twice.

cases.name: reply_below_seam_ignored_even_when_window_has_room
cases.why: Guards against 'only apply the seam when the window is full' — an already-counted reply stays out regardless of room.

cases.name: empty_scope_ingests_first_reply_seam_stays_zero
cases.why: No snapshot was ever loaded, so the seam is 0 — and a live frame must never move it.

cases.name: evicted_live_reply_replay_is_noop
cases.why: @Android-Developer-2's find. Window holds only N: after 6,7,8,9 the reply m-6 is EVICTED. A replayed frame for m-6 is no longer found by a window-scoped identity check, and its seq is above the seam — so a model that derives the count takes the 'new' branch and DOUBLE-COUNTS, and returns a fresh object. Correct: window unchanged, count unchanged, SAME reference.
